title: What does the bigger angle on the other side measure?
description: Two rays from one vertex cut a full turn into a smaller angle and a bigger angle. The smaller angle is taken away from the full turn to find the bigger one. Keeko doubts that the bigger angle has a measure because a protractor stops at one hundred eighty.
teaching_notes: One idea: the two angles at a vertex fill the full turn of three hundred sixty degrees, so the reflex angle is the full turn take away the smaller angle. Watch for students who think a reflex angle cannot be measured.

source: The smaller angle at a vertex is 100°. What is the reflex angle on the other side?
video_script.why: The child sees that the reflex angle is the rest of the full turn once the smaller angle is taken away.
video_script.substitution: Take the smaller angle away from the full turn of 360 degrees.
video_script.anchor: two rays from one vertex, with the smaller angle and the bigger angle on the other side marked by arcs
video_script.wrong_answer: a reflex angle has no measure, because a protractor stops at one hundred eighty
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko says a reflex angle has no measure because a protractor stops at one hundred eighty. The protractor reads only the smaller angle, and the rest of the full turn is still an angle with a measure.
video_script.payoff_line: The reflex angle is two hundred sixty degrees
never_show: a reflex angle has no measure
maths_rules: smaller angle + bigger angle = full turn
260 is more than 180 and less than 360, so it is a reflex angle
video_script.design: One vertex, two rays; the smaller angle is shaded teal and the bigger angle amber. The full turn stays drawn as a circle round the vertex.
